resolve-library-id.rationale: The tool returns matching libraries for a package/product search, including fields such as `Library ID`, `Name`, `Description`, and `Versions`. Because it searches public/open-world library metadata (`Resolves a package/product name` and `returns matching libraries`) and is marked as open-world, attacker-controlled packages or documentation entries can influence returned names/descriptions/IDs. It is not SECRET because no private user data is advertised. It is not a SINK because although `The query is sent to the Context7 API`, that is a fixed vendor endpoint rather than an agent-chosen attacker-readable destination.

query-docs.rationale: The tool `Retrieves and queries up-to-date documentation and code examples` for `any programming library or framework`. Public library documentation and code examples may be authored by outside parties, so returned documentation is attacker-controllable. It is not SECRET because it only advertises retrieval of documentation/code examples, not private user data. It is not a SINK because although `The query is sent to the Context7 API`, that is a fixed vendor endpoint, and `libraryId` is a Context7 identifier such as `/org/project`, not an agent-chosen URL or host.
